claims.text: As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy films form an ordered single-phase hexagonal structure at the baseline substrate temperature.
The baseline FeMnNiGeSi-type films undergo a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition.
The baseline FeMnNiGeSi-type films exhibit significant transition hysteresis.
Changing substrate temperature during deposition changes the density and spatial distribution of nanoscale precipitates or disorder features.
The nanoscale precipitate or disorder distribution governs nucleation and growth kinetics of the magnetostructural transition.
Microstructural tuning through substrate temperature can broaden the magnetocaloric response and reduce hysteresis under low applied fields.
Substrate temperature controls adatom mobility during thin-film deposition.
Changes in adatom mobility modify the formation and spatial distribution of nanoscale precipitates.
An optimal precipitate distribution reduces heterogeneity in nucleation barriers across the film.
Reducing heterogeneity in nucleation barriers moderates transition abruptness and minimizes hysteretic energy losses.
At an optimal substrate temperature, the magnetic entropy change will be moderate and distributed over a wider temperature range than in the baseline film.
At an optimal substrate temperature, transition hysteresis will be significantly lower than in the baseline film.
The predicted effect applies to as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type films under low magnetic fields near the transition temperature.
Substrate temperatures that are too high or too low may produce alternative phases or additional defects.
Residual stress may independently influence the magnetocaloric response.
Unintentional compositional gradients may independently influence the magnetocaloric response.
